papers.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).

papers.title: Magnetic Reconnection Modifies Cosmic-Ray Transport in the Interstellar Medium
papers.abstract: We present numerical magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of the interstellar medium in gravity-stratified boxes with the Piernik MHD code. The system contains thermal gas, spectrally resolved cosmic-ray (CR) nuclei within the CRESP algorithm, and spectrally unresolved CR protons. CR protons drive gas outflows and undergo Coulomb and hadronic losses. CR nuclei undergo Coulomb losses. We also include the spallation of primary Carbon by thermal gas atoms, thereby decaying Car- bon into secondary stable Boron isotopes. We use the resistive-MHD approximation as a subgrid model for unresolved turbulent magnetic dissipation in current sheets. We perform a parameter study of the magnetic diffusivity {\eta}. The Boron-to-Carbon ratio B/C and hadronic {\gamma}-ray luminosity density are computed as diagnostics. We find that non-zero magnetic diffusivity modifies the magnetic topology, leading to a more horizontal field in the halo, thereby accumulating CRs in the disk region and signifi- cantly increasing the CR escape time. As a consequence, the local turbulent conditions and turbulent reconnection in the interstellar medium should be considered when interpreting B/C and hadronic {\gamma}-ray luminosity observed at Earth. Our results suggest that the escape time and diffusion coefficient of CRs deduced from observational data in the vicinity of the Solar System cannot be extrapolated to the whole Galaxy.

papers.title: Tracking the Evolution of Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with Pulsar Terms
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays will soon be able to resolve the loudest supermassive black hole binaries contributing to the stochastic gravitational wave background at nanohertz frequencies. While the few decades of observations are typically not enough to see these binaries evolve in frequency, the so-called pulsar terms offer a glimpse into the past and can help us map out the frequency evolution of these binaries over tens of thousands of years. Measuring this long-term frequency evolution can allow us to look for deviations from a vacuum binary evolution due to various environmental effects. We develop a Fisher-matrix approach to calculate how precisely the frequency can be tracked over time in this manner, and demonstrate its use on a realistic near-future pulsar timing array with a 30-year baseline. We find that the environmental effects predicted by 2-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of circumbinary disks are unlikely to be detectable in the circular binaries we considered, however, in some cases they might result in biased chirp mass recovery if ignored. We also demonstrate how this approach allows one to test the orbital evolution predicted by general relativity in a purely gravitational-wave driven inspiral, and to put upper limits on additional generic environmental effects described by a power-law hardening model.

papers.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
papers.abstract: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.

papers.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
papers.abstract: The origin of the excess of GeV gamma-rays in the Milky Way's galactic center observed by Fermi-LAT has been an open question for nearly two decades. The two leading interpretations of this signal are that it is produced either by annihilating dark matter (DM), or arises from unresolved point sources, such as a novel population of millisecond pulsars. In both scenarios, uncertainties and limitations in the modeling of galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, such as the steady-state approximation of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and assumption of an axisymmetric distribution of CRs, complicate the interpretation of the galactic center excess (GCE). Simulations with full magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and CR transport can provide a new avenue for understanding the astrophysical phenomena that drive galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission. We utilize MHD simulations of Milky Way analogs with time-dependent, spectrally-resolved CR transport to reconstruct diffuse gamma-ray emission. Comparing instantaneous emission to a time-averaged baseline, we find residuals up to several times larger than the Fermi GCE, with a wide range of spectral shapes and spatial morphologies. At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.

papers.title: One-Million-Year-Old Nascent Eclipsing Binaries in the LMC
papers.abstract: The light curves of nascent eclipsing binaries (EBs) feature sinusoidal reflection effects as a hot B-type main-sequence (MS) primary irradiates the near side of a cool, low-mass, pre-MS companion. We obtained multi-epoch echelle spectra with the MIKE spectrograph on the 6.5m Magellan-Clay Telescope of three nascent EBs embedded in H II regions within the LMC. By fitting atmospheric models to the spectra, the primaries are found to be mid-B dwarfs (T_eff,1 = 18,600-22,800 K; M_1 = 6.8-8.5 Msun). The dynamical masses of the secondaries are only M_2 = 0.38-0.95 Msun, yielding extremely small mass ratios q = M_2/M_1 = 0.05-0.11. Unlike solar-type primaries, which exhibit a dearth of close companions with q < 0.1 known as the brown dwarf desert, massive stars can readily form with very close companions below q < 0.1. By fitting PHOEBE models to the OGLE-III light curves, we measure the secondary radii R_2 = 2.0-2.8 Rsun and temperatures T_eff,2 = 4,000 K. The pre-MS companions are located high on the Hayashi track where evolutionary models indicate ages of only 1 Myr. Their extreme youth suggests that nascent EBs formed via inward disk migration during the previous embedded protostellar phase.

papers.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
papers.abstract: We present 14 optical imaging and eight optical spectroscopic epochs of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Keck/LRIS and Gemini/GMOS, two near-infrared (NIR) imaging epochs from Keck/MOSFIRE, and four NIR spectroscopic epochs from Gemini/Flamingos-2 and GNIRS, obtained between 2025 July and 2026 May. Mean GMOS colors of $g-r=0.732\pm0.029$, $r-i=0.237\pm0.025$, and $i-z=0.109\pm0.022$ mag show no significant change across perihelion. Phase-corrected red-band activity follows $Af\rho\propto r_h^{-2.10\pm0.14}$ inbound and $r_h^{-3.34\pm0.43}$ outbound. Transverse-width and sunward-plume speeds imply dust losses of $2.7\times10^9$ and $1.0\times10^{10}$ kg over 2025 July 3--2026 May 15 for 1-$\mu$m--1-mm grains, equivalent to global layers of 0.26 and 0.99 m under the adopted grain and nucleus assumptions. The concentrated coma, compact sunward feature, and antisolar tail seen on 2025 August 27 broadened by 2025 November 26; extended dust persisted through 2026 February 17. C$_2$/CN nearly doubled from $0.257\pm0.014$ on 2025 September 14--15 to $0.481\pm0.080$ on 2025 November 26, while C$_3$/CN fell from $0.327\pm0.024$ on 2025 August 28 to $0.214\pm0.009$ on 2025 September 14--15. MOSFIRE NIR imaging on 2025 July 11 gives $Y-J=0.466\pm0.143$, $J-H=0.239\pm0.052$, $H-K_s=0.454\pm0.150$, and $J-K_s=0.693\pm0.202$ mag. Spectra give $J-H=0.24$ mag on 2025 September 5--6 and $J-H=0.27$--0.28 and $J-K_s=0.21$--0.22 mag on 2025 December 1--2 over the retained passband intervals. Model-calibrated imaging on 2026 February 6 gives near-solar $J-K_s=0.303\pm0.051$ mag. No water-ice absorption is robust to the tested continuum and calibration choices in the NIR spectra. These observations provide a lasting record of the comet's evolution through the Solar System and a benchmark for studying and monitoring future interstellar objects.

papers.title: Natural Inflation with Exponentially Small Tensor-To-Scalar Ratio
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that "natural inflation", also known as "axion inflation", can be compatible with Planck 2018 measurements of the cosmic microwave background, while predicting an exponentially small tensor-to-scalar ratio, e.g., $r\sim 10^{-15}$. The strong suppression of $r$ arises from dynamics of the radial component of the complex scalar field, whose phase is the axion. Such tiny values of $r$ remain well below the threshold for detection by CMB-S4 or Simons Observatory B-mode searches. The model is testable with the running $\alpha_s$ of the spectral index, which is within reach of next-generation CMB and large-scale structure experiments, motivating the running as a primary science goal for future experiments.
papers.comments: 5 pages, 3 figures. v2: matches version published in PRD

papers.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- Ultracool dwarfs in the Euclid Deep Fields
papers.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) encompass the lowest-mass stars and brown dwarfs at the substellar boundary. These intrinsically faint objects are challenging to detect, but the wide coverage and deep sensitivity of the Euclid survey increase confirmed UCD counts by orders of magnitude. We carried out a systematic study using Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) low-resolution near-infrared spectra to identify and characterise UCDs. A sample of previously known UCDs in Q1 validated the analysis, which was then applied to newly identified UCD candidates in Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N; 22.9 deg^2, down to J_E ~ 24.5 mag). We confirm 33 new UCDs in EDF-N, spanning spectral types M7-T1 (J_E = 17-21 mag) and distances of 50-600 pc. Two objects were followed up with optical and NIR observations using the Gran Telescopio Canarias, providing independent validation of Euclid classifications. We determined spectral types for 33 new UCDs and 167 previously known UCDs by fitting SpeX Prism Library Analysis Toolkit standards. The known sample includes 103 Dark Energy Survey objects (M7-T0, J_E = 17-22 mag), 6 literature sources (M8-T7, J_E = 18-20 mag), and 58 Gaia sources (M7-L1, J_E = 17-24 mag). Independent stellar parameters from atmospheric model fitting agree well with Euclid spectral types. We also investigated Gaia UCDs in Q1 by combining mean XP spectra with Euclid NIR spectra to determine radii. We present a publicly available catalogue including observations, classifications, and stellar parameters. This work demonstrates Euclid's capability to characterise faint stellar populations, establishing a foundation for large-scale UCD studies.

papers.title: Resilience of Primordial Black Hole Formation from Inflation with a Light Spectator Field
papers.abstract: Scalar fields are ubiquitous in theories of high-energy physics. In the context of cosmic inflation, this suggests the existence of spectator fields, which provide a subdominant source of energy density. We show that spectator fields boost the inflationary production of primordial black holes, with single-field ultra-slow-roll evolution supplanted by a phase of evolution along the spectator direction, and primordial perturbations amplified by the resulting multifield dynamics. This generic mechanism is largely free from the severe fine-tuning that afflicts single-field inflationary PBH models.

papers.title: Tracing the evolution of eccentric precessing binary black holes: a hybrid approach
papers.abstract: To describe a general bound binary black hole system, we need to consider orbital eccentricity and the misalignment of black holes' spin vectors with respect to the orbital angular momentum. Binary black holes often have a non-negligible eccentricity at formation, and dynamical interactions could produce binaries with non-negligible eccentricity in the bands of gravitational-wave (GW) detectors. The angle between each black hole's spin vector and the binary's orbital angular momentum (referred to as the spin tilt) at formation also carries information about the formation channel. The spin tilts inferred in GW astronomy are usually those when the binary is in the band of a GW detector. Therefore, it is necessary to evolve the binary back in time to compute the tilts at formation. For certain binaries, the tilts in the formal limit of infinite orbital angular momentum, also known as tilts at infinity, could be a useful approximation to those at formation. Additionally, full orbit-averaged evolution to formation could be computationally infeasible in many situations, while the hybrid evolution we use to compute the tilts at infinity would be feasible. We thus generalize the publicly available tilts_at_infinity code to compute the tilts at infinity for eccentric, spin-precessing binaries. This code employs hybrid post-Newtonian evolution, starting with orbit-averaged evolution for higher frequencies and then transitioning to precession-averaged evolution to compute the tilts at infinity. We find that the transition frequency used in the quasicircular case still gives acceptably small errors in the eccentric case, and show that eccentricity and hybrid evolution both have a significant effect on the tilts at infinity for many binaries. We also give examples of cases where the tilts at infinity are and are not a good approximation to the tilts at formation in the eccentric case. (Abridged)
papers.comments: Revised after peer review and accepted for publication in Physical Review D

papers.title: Inverse reconstruction of Einstein cluster collapse and oscillations in tangential-pressure spacetimes
papers.abstract: We formulate an inverse reconstruction procedure for spherically symmetric Datta--Bondi--Gair spacetimes with vanishing radial pressure and non-zero tangential pressure supported by angular momentum. Extending the logic of Krasiński--Hellaby reconstruction for Lemaître--Tolman--Bondi dust, we determine the full, exact space-time information from prescribed density, velocity or equilibrium state. Two specific constructions are developed. The first represents an initially expanding fluid with a finite turnaround, followed by an asymptotic collapse to an unstable Einstein cluster configuration. In the second, a static equilibrium density and a finite time density-velocity pair determine finite amplitude oscillations around a stable Einstein cluster. Numerical examples use a Jaffe-type final profile and an Einasto equilibrium with an approximate Navarro--Frenk--White finite time profile. The latter admits many oscillations before the first shell crossing is detected. The constructions provide diagnostics of the admissibility of prescribed configurations.
papers.comments: 30 pages. Revised manuscript with clarifications to the reconstruction procedures, regularity conditions and numerical analysis

papers.title: Primordial Black Holes from Inflation with a Spectator Field
papers.abstract: How is the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) in single-field models of inflation impacted by the presence of additional scalar fields? We consider the effect of a spectator field - a free scalar field with sub-Hubble mass and no direct coupling to the inflaton and which makes a subdominant contribution to the total energy density - in the context of single-field models of inflation featuring a transient phase of ultra-slow-roll evolution. Despite the modest title, a spectator field can have a dramatic impact: the slow-roll evolution of the spectator prevents the combined inflaton-and-spectator system from entering into ultra-slow-roll, which naively might be expected to preclude the production of PBHs. However, we demonstrate that the growth of perturbations is maintained or enhanced by the spectator, through the rich interplay of curvature and isocurvature perturbations. We show in a model-independent way that the single-field phase of ultra-slow-roll is replaced by two turns in field space encompassing a phase of tachyonic instability for the isocurvature perturbations and a transfer of power from isocurvature to curvature modes. Furthermore, we highlight a degeneracy between the fine-tuning of the feature in the inflaton potential and the parameters of the spectator, leading to an overall resilience of model predictions to parameter variations. This makes it easier for the underlying PBH model to accommodate both high-precision cosmic microwave background constraints and production of PBHs in the asteroid-mass range.

papers.title: Cosmological Equivalence of Scalar-Tensor-Vector Modified Gravity and Cold Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We show that Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity (STVG-MOG) is observationally equivalent to the standard model $\Lambda$CDM cosmological model for all probes that depend on isotropic and linear gravitational dynamics, including galaxy rotation curves, cluster lensing, the linear matter power spectrum P(k), $\sigma_8$, baryon acoustic oscillations, and the cosmic microwave background (CMB). This degeneracy arises from the scale-dependent effective gravitational coupling $G_{\mathrm{eff}}$, which ensures identical background evolution, transfer functions, and linear growth. Consequently, all early-universe, low and intermediate scale cosmological observables are equally well described by STVG-MOG without invoking non-baryonic dark matter. We argue that the equivalence implies that isotropic cosmological data alone cannot establish the physical existence of dark matter. The degeneracy is broken only by observables sensitive to large-scale, anisotropic gravitational response. In particular, recent measurements of enhanced radio-galaxy and quasar number-count dipoles at gigaparsec scales probe a regime where $G_{\mathrm{eff}}$ departs from its $\Lambda$CDM limit, allowing STVG-MOG to generate anisotropic bulk flows, while preserving consistency with all isotropic constraints. These observations provide a concrete pathway for empirically distinguishing modified gravity from particle dark matter.
papers.comments: 11 pages. No figures

papers.title: Kinematic cosmic dipole from a large sample of strong lenses
papers.abstract: Measurements of the kinematic cosmic dipole continue to show an intriguing tension between the value inferred from the CMB and that obtained from high-redshift source number counts. While the measured dipole direction appears consistent, the amplitude, set by the observer's peculiar velocity $v_{o}$, remains in significant disagreement. In this paper, we propose using strong gravitational lenses with well-measured Einstein radii to estimate the kinematic cosmic dipole, through the relativistic aberration of the Einstein angle induced by the observer's motion. We show that this effect could be detected solely from measurements of the Einstein radius in wide, high-resolution imaging surveys such as Euclid. However, the precision achievable using Einstein-radius measurements alone, without redshift or lens-galaxy mass information, appears insufficient to discriminate between the CMB value of $v_{o}$ and that derived from source number counts at high statistical significance. Nevertheless, we demonstrate that including a large sample of lenses with available kinematic information, either via the Fundamental Plane relation or, ideally, through spectroscopic velocity-dispersion measurements, drastically reduces the noise and substantially improves the constraining power of this method. We show that, for a realistic sample of strong lenses detected by Euclid and complemented with spectroscopic velocity dispersion measurements from 4MOST or DESI, it is possible to discriminate between the CMB- and source-number-counts-inferred values at the $\sim 5\sigma$ level using a new, fully independent method. We further demonstrate that this technique is only weakly sensitive to strong-lensing selection effects, with selection biases and threshold effects estimated to be well below the 1% level.
papers.comments: 19 pages + 4 Appendices, 5 figures, 4 tables. Published in JCAP

papers.title: Dark Matter, Baryon Number, and Cosmic-Ray Antinuclei
papers.abstract: Antideuterons and antihelium nuclei in the cosmic-ray spectrum have long been considered a smoking gun signature of dark matter annihilation, making the tentative observation of several such events by AMS highly intriguing. Conventional dark matter models, however, can produce only up to O(1) antideuteron events at AMS and are not capable of generating observable fluxes of antihelium. In this Letter, we propose a class of models in which dark matter annihilates into particles carrying baryon and lepton number, whose subsequent decays produce enhanced fluxes of antinucleons and antinuclei. Such scenarios are motivated by Grand Unified Theories and can lead to an order-of-magnitude or larger enhancement in the resulting antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes, providing a means by which to potentially explain the events reported by the AMS Collaboration.
papers.comments: 8 pages, 6 figures; v2: updated to journal version

papers.title: Spin the black circle II: tidal heating and torquing of a rotating black hole by a test mass on generic orbits
papers.abstract: Horizon fluxes of energy and angular momentum are a key strong-field effect in the dynamics of black holes, encoding direct information about their nature. In this work, we present a numerical study of these fluxes for a test particle orbiting a Kerr black hole on equatorial geodesics, covering circular, eccentric, and hyperbolic trajectories across a wide range of orbital parameters and black hole spins. We reproduce known results for circular orbits and uncover a richer phenomenology for eccentric and hyperbolic ones: the instantaneous fluxes can exhibit multiple peaks and sign changes, indicating a complex interplay between orbital dynamics and horizon perturbation. We then compare these results against existing analytical post-Newtonian expressions, exploring resummation strategies to improve their performance against numerical data. In particular, we propose a factorized and resummed representation of the horizon fluxes that predicts the onset frequency of the superradiant regime to within $10\%$ for $\gtrsim 83\%$ for both the energy and angular momentum fluxes of bound configurations; high-energy open orbits however remain a challenge. This representation exactly reduces to the circular limit by construction, independently of the perturbative order of the remaining analytical terms. For peak and orbit-averaged fluxes, the analytical models achieve acceptable accuracy -- with relative errors at the $10\%$ level or below -- at large separations and low eccentricities. However, they can exhibit deviations of $\sim \mathcal{O}(100\%)$ in the strong-field regime, motivating the need for improved flux prescriptions and further investigations.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 12 figures; version accepted for publication

papers.title: Absorption and scattering spectra of massive scalar waves in charged regular black hole spacetimes
papers.abstract: Regular black holes (RBHs) can be seen as possible alternatives to standard black holes (BHs), since these geometries do not have a curvature singularity. As a way of improving our knowledge of such geometries, we can investigate how the astrophysical environment interacts with RBHs and compare the results with those obtained in the framework of standard BHs. In this work, we aim to study the absorption and scattering cross sections of massive scalar waves impinging on Ayón-Beato-García and Bardeen charged RBH geometries, focusing on understanding the role played by the field's mass. Concerning the absorption spectrum, our numerical results show that the total absorption cross section decreases as we increase the field's mass for fixed values of the BH charge. In turn, in the scattering spectrum, an increase in the mass of the field leads to wider interference widths for field velocities larger than a critical value, $v_c$. Moreover, we also compare our numerical results with the classical and semiclassical approximations, showing that they agree very well within the appropriate limits. We also draw comparisons with the results of the Reissner-Nordström metric. In particular, we show that the mass of the field contributes to finding situations in which the absorption and scattering spectra of regular and standard BHs are similar for arbitrary values of the field frequency and scattering angle, considering low- to near-extreme BH charges.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 16 figures

papers.title: Toward Bayesian photometric cosmic chronometers: Application to VIPERS
papers.abstract: The cosmic chronometer (CC) method provides a direct measurement of the expansion history of the universe, $H(z)$, from the differential ages of passively evolving galaxies. However, most CC analyses rely on high-quality spectroscopy to select passive galaxies, measure age-sensitive spectral features, and control stellar-population systematics. We build on existing works that use the D4000 spectral break as a proxy for measuring galaxy ages and apply it to a photometry-selected galaxy sample from VIPERS PDR2 in the range $0.5 \le z \le 0.8$. Our goal is to extend the scope of the standard CC framework to photometric surveys. To achieve this, we first selected a massive and passive galaxy sample using rest-frame colors and mass. Second, we designed a Bayesian framework to infer full galaxy age posteriors in fine redshift bins, using a D4000-age-metallicity grid from stellar population synthesis models. We marginalized over metallicity, using a Gaussian metallicity prior to break the D4000-age-metallicity degeneracy. Subsequently, we derived age-difference posteriors between redshift bins by convolving their age posteriors. Finally, using the median and errors extracted from the differential age posteriors, we calculated the weighted average $H(z)$ over our selected redshift range. We obtain $H(z=0.65)=93.68\pm28.27\,{\rm (stat.)}\pm10.67\,{\rm (syst.)}\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, which is consistent with existing spectroscopic CC measurements and with the $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda$CDM) model prediction from Planck at the same redshift. This result provides a proof of concept for extending direct $H(z)$ measurements from cosmic chronometers to photometric and spectro-photometric surveys, where larger samples can compensate for lower spectral resolution, provided that passive-galaxy selection, metallicity priors, and stellar-population systematics are carefully controlled.
papers.comments: 22 pages, 16 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.title: Higher Dimensional Loop Quantum Black hole in de Sitter Spacetime: Quasinormal Modes and Shadow Signatures
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamical and optical properties of a higher-dimensional loop-quantum-corrected black hole in a de Sitter background. We first analyze the horizon structure and identify the admissible nonextremal black-hole domain bounded by the extremal and Nariai configurations, ensuring the existence of distinct inner, event, and cosmological horizons for the parameter sets considered. We then examine the scalar effective potential and show that the loop-quantum correction deforms the classical scattering barrier primarily in the strong-field region while preserving its characteristic single-barrier structure. The quasinormal modes of massless scalar perturbations are computed using time-domain evolution with Prony extraction, the matrix method, and the WKB approximation, showing good agreement among the three approaches. The time-domain waveform and its Prony and matrix-frequency reconstructions provide an additional direct consistency check of the extracted ringdown spectrum. We find that loop quantum corrections induce moderate shifts in the quasinormal spectrum, whereas the spacetime dimensionality has a much stronger impact, leading to higher oscillation frequencies and damping rates. The negative imaginary parts of all modes indicate dynamical stability against massless scalar perturbations within the explored parameter range. Comparison with the corresponding classical black-hole backgrounds shows that the quantum-corrected quasinormal spectrum remains continuously connected to the classical photon-sphere branch, with the loop correction producing quantitative rather than qualitative changes.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 12 figures and 5 tables Accepted for publication in EPJC

papers.title: UCLCHEM 4.0: An open source gas-grain astrochemistry simulation framework
papers.abstract: Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations enabled by modern day observational facilities. UCLCHEM is a comprehensive gas-grain astrochemical modelling framework that can compute the chemical evolution inside a parcel of gas and dust under a specified, time-dependent physical description. This allows both the post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and the usage of physical parametrizations, ranging in context from extra-galactic to protoplanetary disk scales. The framework consists of a core routine that solves gas-grain chemical reaction networks as a function of time, self-consistently coupled to either a user-defined or parametrized physical evolution of density, temperature and other physical input parameters. The chemistry is solved with a rate-equation formalism, and includes a three phase description, namely gas phase, ice surface and bulk ice. This includes transport between the gas and ice phases via freeze-out, thermal and non-thermal desorption mechanisms, as well as a geometrical treatment of the growth and shrinkage of the surface and bulk chemistry. The framework includes parametrizations for astrochemical modelling of cloud collapses, protostellar cores and shocks as well as the ability to provide user-defined inputs. This release of the framework focuses on many quality-of-life-improvements, including an object-oriented Python interface, an upgrade from two phase to three phases and expanded support for post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and user-defined parametrizations. This manuscript provides an overview of the physics and chemistry included in UCLCHEM, as well as the inner workings of the solver routine and the programming interface.

papers.title: Chaotic behaviors of particles around the black hole with an anisotropic matter immersed in a magnetic field
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations that describes a static black hole coexisting with anisotropic matter immersed in an external magnetic field, obtained via the Harrison transformation. Our findings reveal that an increase in the anisotropic matter parameter systematically suppresses the local chaotic behavior, as indicated by a reduction in the Lyapunov exponent. Conversely, variations in the external magnetic field lead to qualitative changes in global chaotic behavior. This is analyzed through Poincaré sections, which demonstrate transitions between regular and chaotic trajectories resulting from the nonlinear gravitational-magnetic interactions. These factors play distinct yet complementary roles in shaping chaotic particle dynamics around black holes. This study would offer a new theoretical framework for exploring nonintegrable particle motion within magnetized black hole spacetimes.

papers.title: Exploring Exact Einsteinian Black Hole Physics in Dark Matter Environment: Ray Tracing, Stability, Eikonal QNMs and Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent rebuttal of black hole--dark matter solutions based on velocity-matching, we reconstruct the spacetime by treating the dark matter halo density directly as an energy-density source in the Einstein field equations. We obtain an exact static, spherically symmetric black hole solution and investigate the effects of the halo on its geometry, optical properties, quasinormal modes, and thermodynamics. Using null geodesics, we show that the halo modifies photon trajectories, shifts the circular photon orbit, and enlarges the photon sphere and apparent shadow. The Lyapunov exponent of the unstable null orbit further determines the eikonal quasinormal modes, yielding explicit halo-induced corrections to their oscillation and damping rates. We also compute the mass, Hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, and Gibbs free energy to characterize the thermodynamic stability and phase structure. We find that the dark matter halo enlarges the domain of thermodynamic stability and introduces nontrivial phase behavior absent in the Schwarzschild case, demonstrating that astrophysical dark matter environments can leave potentially observable imprints on black hole observables.

papers.title: Even central galaxies feel their environment: cosmic siphoning of cool gas accretion
papers.abstract: Identifying the key processes regulating cool gas accretion in galaxies is essential for understanding the baryon cycle within galactic ecosystems. Recent studies indicate that the most fundamental internal process is likely the competition between halos and central black holes. This is revealed through a universal relation between increasing black hole masses and decreasing cool gas fraction ($\mu_{\rm HI} \equiv M_{\rm HI}/M_{\star} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{-0.6}$). Here we further explore the primary external effects on cool gas accretion in central galaxies. We find that galaxies deviating significantly from the $\mu_{\rm HI}-M_{\rm BH}$ relation are overwhelmingly isolated central galaxies without substantial satellites. These isolated, gas-poor centrals exhibit systematically higher black-hole-to-stellar-mass ratios and more prominent bulges. At larger scales, they are preferentially located near massive neighboring halos. We suggest that this may reflect a ``cosmic siphoning" scenario, replenished by their satellites and by gas flowing along the cosmic web. This model naturally explains the prevalence of gas-poor isolated central galaxies near massive halos. It complements internal regulation by supermassive black holes and suggests a cosmic 'rich get richer' scenario.

papers.title: A Spectral Criterion for Emergent Gravity
papers.abstract: We give a source-resolved spectral criterion for long-range tensor exchange between conserved matter sources. Exact channel elimination preserves the propagation kernel together with the source and readout maps and the direct response. Common-space estimates control the residue at the displaced critical root of a finite approximation. A positive Källen-Lehmann representation identifies this residue with a zero-invariant-mass atom even at a continuum endpoint. For a complete positive Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor we classify the null-shell measure and prove that its TT atomic weight vanishes. A reduced compact spectral realisation instead carries internal tensor vertices into an external two-helicity response. Conservation reduces the leading vertex of localised stationary matter to its total energy. The mixed residue then factorises into the two energies and a common propagation coefficient. Spatial resolvent estimates determine the potential and force with finite-size corrections. Normalisation through the matter vertex leaves one dimensional calibration for the overall Planck scale. The spectral residue fixes the dimensionless exchange strength. The resulting response admits an Einstein-matter effective description under the stated positivity and helicity assumptions together with universal soft coupling and local nonlinear consistency.

papers.title: Extra-dimensional Origins of Chemical Potentials at the Cosmological Collider
papers.abstract: We study the realization of the chemical potential mechanism in cosmological collider physics in a robust class of inflationary models arising from multiple higher-dimensional gauge fields. The rolling inflaton background corresponds to an electric field in the extra dimension in which charged particles are produced analogously to the Schwinger mechanism, while neutral particles can be produced through non-minimal interactions. We show that particles heavier than the inflationary Hubble scale can be created without Boltzmann suppression in both cases. In particular, charged Kaluza-Klein excitations can be created through minimal gauge interactions. We construct realistic models along these lines consistent with both theoretical and experimental constraints.

papers.title: Effective reheating in Gauss--Bonnet inflation with $μ(ϕ,X)$ coupling
papers.abstract: We study effective reheating in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet inflationary model with a phase-space-dependent coupling $\mu(\phi,X)$, in which a compact field-space feature is combined with a bounded kinetic gate. The modified inflationary background determines the pivot-scale quantities and the effective energy density at the end of inflation. These quantities are then used to derive the reheating duration $N_{\rm re}$ and temperature $T_{\rm re}$ through the thermal-history matching relation. We first perform two fixed-pivot reference scans by varying the overall Gauss--Bonnet strength $\lambda_{\rm GB}$ and the kinetic parameter $g_{_X}$ separately. For the reference parameter choices, increasing either parameter increases $N_{\rm re}$ and decreases $T_{\rm re}$ for the selected reheating equations of state. Additional benchmark calculations clarify how these variations depend on the dynamical regime of the model. In the $\lambda_{\rm GB}$ scan, the increase in $N_{\rm re}$ and the decrease in $T_{\rm re}$ persist, although both variations become strongly suppressed when the coupling is more localized or when the end of inflation is controlled more strongly by the E-model potential. In the $g_{_X}$ scan, stronger field-space localization and kinetic saturation can instead lead to a slight decrease in $N_{\rm re}$ and an increase in $T_{\rm re}$ as $g_{_X}$ is increased. When the bounded kinetic contribution is considered together with a weaker overall Gauss--Bonnet interaction, the resulting changes in the reheating quantities become nearly negligible. The fixed-pivot predictions of the representative and alternative benchmarks are compared with CMB this http URL reheating constraints are then discussed for four representative values of the effective equation-of-state parameter, $\overline{w}_{\rm re}=-1/3,0,2/3,$ and $1$.

papers.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
papers.abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. The final model attains a validation precision of 0.919, recall of 0.905, and $F_1$ of 0.912, and yields 29,605 dual-nucleus candidates after removing star-dominated and blended detections. Structured visual inspection indicates that $54.5$--$62\%$ are consistent with genuine dual nuclei, implying $\sim(1.4$--$1.8)\times10^{4}$ plausible systems. Cross-calibrating the YOLO separation against the deterministic GOTHIC centroid measurement and restricting to the compact regime ($d \le 6.87''$) gives a conservative subset of $\sim 13{,}672$ candidates, reaching calibrated separations of $\sim 0.56''$. Spectroscopy of the most compact ($\le 1$ kpc) systems shows spectra dominated by stellar absorption, with no resolved double-peaked emission, so confirmation requires higher-resolution follow-up. The catalogue is a statistically refined list of candidates, not confirmed DAGN. Nonetheless, deep-learning detection substantially reduces contamination and expands the plausible DAGN census.

papers.title: AXIS Could Have Accessed Dark Matter Decays
papers.abstract: The Advanced X-ray Imaging Satellite (AXIS) was a mission concept designed to improve upon the sensitivity and spatial resolution of the Chandra X-ray Observatory and XMM-Newton. Although AXIS was not selected for implementation, the concept study defined a mature instrument design with low-background, arcsecond imaging over the $0.3$-$10$ keV energy range, a large effective area, and a wide field of view. These capabilities provide a useful benchmark for the dark matter decay sensitivity of future X-ray observatories. We estimate the reach of a future AXIS-like instrument for narrow photon lines from decaying keV-scale dark matter, including axion-like particles and sterile neutrinos. For Galactic center observations, we find projected lifetime sensitivities of order $10^{31}$ s, improving upon existing limits by up to an order of magnitude over part of the keV mass range.
papers.comments: 8 pages, 5 figures

papers.title: Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations
papers.abstract: Reconstructing the initial conditions of the Universe from late-time tracers would unlock cosmological information buried by non-linear structure formation and astrophysics. We reconstruct the initial density field corresponding to $z=300$, with its linear amplitude extrapolated to $z=0$, from simulated 21-cm and CO(1-0) line-intensity maps at $z=8$ generated with LIMFAST. Using a three-dimensional U-Net, we reconstruct the initial conditions and evaluate their impact on cosmological parameter constraints. The two tracers probe complementary environments: 21-cm emission traces neutral, low-density regions of the IGM, while CO traces overdense, star-forming regions. We also train and evaluate the reconstruction on maps incorporating SKA1-Low- and COMAP-ERA-like instrumental response and thermal noise. In the noiseless case, combining both tracers delivers the most accurate reconstruction across ionisation states, with the cross-correlation coefficient between the reconstructed and true initial density fields, $|C(k)| \gtrsim 0.90$ for $k \lesssim 0.75\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. With observational effects, small-scale information is degraded, but the joint reconstruction retains substantial large-scale coherence, with $|C(k)| \gtrsim 0.70$ for $k \lesssim 0.3\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We quantify cosmological information gains through simulation-based inference using power-spectrum summaries pre- and post-reconstruction. The largest improvements occur for $\sigma_8$ and $n_{\rm s}$, with a median aggregate marginal compression of $1.17$ bits in the noiseless case, corresponding to a $56\%$ reduction in the factorised product of prior-normalised $68\%$ marginal widths. With observational effects, the corresponding median compression is $1.29$ bits. These results demonstrate that joint 21-cm-CO reconstruction recovers cosmological information beyond pre-reconstruction summaries.

papers.title: The Loud Tail of the Supermassive Black Hole Binary Population: Multimessenger Candidates and Prospects for SKAO
papers.abstract: We assess whether electromagnetically identified supermassive black hole (SMBH) binary candidates populate the rare, high-amplitude tail of the gravitational wave (GW) amplitude distribution. Using an SMBH binary population model fitted to the NANOGrav 15-year data, we find that 3C~66B and Mrk~501 are likely to stand out from the GW background, making them promising targets for individual-source searches. Furthermore, we show that individual detections can probe the binary hardening mechanism, as models with strong environmental hardening predict a higher abundance of individually resolvable binaries than purely GW-driven models. Applying the same population fits and accounting for the confusion noise from the unresolved population, we forecast that the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will resolve tens of individual binaries, with 3C~66B robustly detectable.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 6 figures

papers.title: Direct detection of right-handed fermionic dark matter: electron-recoil measurements in Xe atoms
papers.abstract: We present theoretical estimations of the event rates for the interaction between a right-handed fermionic dark matter with an electron bound to a xenon atom. Motivated by recent astrophysical and cosmological constraints on a fermionic dark matter candidate in the sub-MeV mass range, we study such an interaction through an effective electromagnetic channel where the output consists of standard-model particles. This mechanism allows right-handed neutral dark matter fermions to couple with standard-model particles with the interchange of $W^{\pm}$ or $Z$ bosons, without the need to add extra fields. We generalize and extend previous results on this type of channels, by including for the ionization form factor arising from the interaction of the fermionic candidate with bound electrons. In addition, we compute the sensitivity curves for different direct detection experiments in such a challenging light particle mass range.

papers.title: Separating the Optical to Near-Infrared Light of AGN and Their Host Galaxies
papers.abstract: The properties of galaxies that host active galactic nuclei (AGNs) offer clues to the conditions that enable accretion onto supermassive black holes. A galaxy's morphology can provide significant information on the evolutionary processes underway. By modeling the surface-brightness profiles of galaxies that host AGN, we can characterize physical properties of the host galaxy. With a sample of sources across a wide range of redshifts, we can investigate how both the supermassive black hole and galaxy evolve over time. Applying the best practices from previous work, we perform Sersic + point source fits of 96 X-ray-selected AGN in the Extended Groth Strip across up to 13 bands of James Webb Space Telescope and Hubble Space Telescope imaging using AstroPhot. We examine both parametric (Sersic) and nonparametric methods in tandem to best determine the physical properties of the host galaxy. After separating the light of the host galaxy and the AGN, we perform independent CIGALE model fits to photometric spectral energy distributions to estimate physical properties including the host galaxy stellar mass and star formation rate, and AGN disk luminosity. In the stellar-mass/star-formation-rate plane, the AGN host galaxies align with the population of massive non-AGN galaxies in the control sample across all redshifts. The AGN disk luminosities result in ratios of bolometric to X-ray flux within the expected range, 5-20:1. We provide an evaluation of the limitations of Sersic modeling to obtain galaxy properties and provide recommendations on best practices for multi-band AGN+host galaxy image decomposition with James Webb Space Telescope imaging.

papers.title: CosmoAgent: AI Agent for Theoretical Cosmology
papers.abstract: We present CosmoAgent, an agentic AI framework using large language models (LLMs) to search for dark-energy and modified-gravity models. We define a covariant grammar that allows LLM agents to explore the space of modified-gravity Lagrangians. An in-house computational pipeline derives the equations of motion, solves the background dynamics, and evaluates the likelihood using late-time expansion data, including the DES 5-year type Ia supernova sample and the DESI Data Release 2 BAO measurements. Theories are ranked by the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to balance simplicity and likelihood. We benchmarked 8 frontier LLMs from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, and Qwen, and all LLMs are able to find theories with a lower nominal AIC than flat $\Lambda$CDM, with a best improvement of $\Delta$ AIC=-3.328. Seven recover quadratic quintessence. Exploratory searches also return induced-gravity and scalar-Gauss-Bonnet structures. The modest AIC improvements do not establish an observational preference for these models over flat $\Lambda$CDM. The code is publicly available at this https URL

papers.title: The DARWIN Project: Cosmological Simulations of Galaxy Formation down to Dwarf Scales in Diverse Environments
papers.abstract: We present the DARWIN project, a suite of cosmological simulations with RAMSES to study dwarf-galaxy formation and evolution across diverse environments. DARWIN-1 is a full-box simulation in a cubic volume of $(65.5\,{\rm cMpc})^3$ with a minimum cell size of 500pc, while DARWIN-2 comprises zoom-in simulations of 24 field regions and a Milky Way analog connected to a filament, reaching 62.5pc resolution. The simulations employ baryonic physics tailored to their aims. For DARWIN-2, we include radiative transfer in three photon energy bands to trace hydrogen and helium ionization. DARWIN-1 reproduces the cosmic star formation rate density and galaxy stellar mass functions reasonably well at $z>1$. Both simulations broadly reproduce observed stellar mass-halo mass relations, chemical abundances, star-formation surface densities, and black hole-galaxy scaling relations. At lower redshift, DARWIN-1 shows an excess in the number density of massive galaxies, although the inferred stellar content of massive halos depends on the definition of galaxy stellar mass. Other systematic differences arise from spatial resolution, feedback efficiency, and environmental selection. To facilitate comparison with observations, we generate mock images using the radiative transfer codes SKIRT and Powderday. We also explore a machine-learning approach to mitigate resolution-driven biases in the dwarf galaxy properties of DARWIN-1 using the higher-resolution DARWIN-2 simulations. The DARWIN simulation suite therefore provides a comprehensive numerical framework for studying the formation, evolution, and internal physics of dwarf galaxies in a cosmological context.

papers.title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: The [C II] Luminosity Function of UV-Selected Galaxies at $z\sim7$
papers.abstract: Luminosity functions (LF) are some of the most basic quantities providing insights into galaxy evolution across cosmic time and enabling a direct comparison between observations and simulations. Here, we present the first [CII]158$\mu$m LF at $z\sim7$ from a sizeable UV-selected ALMA sample. Our analysis makes use of 27 galaxies with significant [CII] emission line detections in the epoch of reionization from the REBELS (Reionization Era Bright Emission Line Survey) ALMA Large Program and its pilot programs. We used these line detections and similar from ALPINE to calibrate UV luminosity-$L_{\mathrm{[CII]}}$ and stellar mass-$L_{\mathrm{[CII]}}$ relations at $z\sim7$. Given the challenge in precisely defining a selection volume for the REBELS sample itself, we rely on published UV LF and stellar mass function (SMF) determinations at $z\sim7$ and three complementary approaches to derive the [CII] LF. The UV LF-based method provides a lower limit on the [CII] LF, due to its missing the most dust-obscured systems. Our SMF-based estimate yields a Schechter function with a characteristic luminosity of $L^*_{\mathrm{[CII]}}=10^{9.11^{+0.11}_{-0.27}} L_\odot$ and a steep faint-end slope. From $z\sim7$ to $z\sim5$, our inferred [CII] LF shows an evolution of +0.3 dex in normalisation and +0.1 dex in $L^*_{\mathrm{[CII]}}$. Our results indicate a general underprediction from models of the abundance of [CII] emitters at high-redshift and thus potentially the number densities of massive yet UV-faint systems implied by our SMF-based method. Additionally, they suggest that 63% of the star formation rate density occurs in massive [CII]-bright systems and that $\sim$60-90% of [CII] emitters at $z\sim7$ may be missed by bright UV selections. This highlights the importance of surveys focusing on especially massive, UV-faint sources at $z>6$.

papers.title: Post-adiabatic effective-one-body waveforms for coalescing compact binaries
papers.abstract: I apply and extend the formalism of osculating orbits of Damour et al. (2004) and Lynch et al. (2026) to eccentric effective one body (EOB) models, in order to obtain an efficient yet accurate description of the inspiral-to-plunge dynamics of tidal, spinning compact binaries, including precessing ones by twisting the otherwise planar motion. The method is recast in terms of equinoctial orbital elements, to circumvent singularities associated with the zero-eccentricity limit. While the formalism is general and can be applied to any EOB model, I focus here on the TEOBResumS-Dalí family and demonstrate how this technique speeds up waveform generation without significantly compromising the accuracy of the model. Over $10^4$ binary neutron stars (BNSs) and as many binary black holes (BBHs) with initial eccentricities up to $0.6$ at $20$ Hz, the median speedup against an optimized version of the model is $\sim 2.6$ for BNSs and $\sim 1.5$ for BBHs, with mismatches against the full numerical solution always below $5 \times 10^{-7}$. The largest speedups, up to $\sim 7$ for individual systems, are obtained for light BBHs ($M \lesssim 8 M_\odot$) with low eccentricities $(e_0 \lesssim 0.1)$. In absolute terms, the median time needed to generate a BNS waveform is $\sim 0.5$ s, with $99.7\%$ of the systems below one second, and for long signals the model is up to $\sim 26$ times faster than a previous version. Applied to the calculation of initial conditions in the $e \rightarrow 0$ limit, the inclusion of radiation-reaction effects allows the model's input eccentricity to agree with the gauge-invariant waveform eccentricity down to initial values of $\sim 7 \times 10^{-8}$. Beyond time-domain applications, the same construction also gives frequency-domain EOB waveforms for eccentric compact binaries via a multi-harmonic stationary phase approximation.

papers.title: A neural-network model to find correlations in astrochemical space
papers.abstract: The detection of new interstellar molecules is central to astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field in past decade has been the increase in both number and diversity of detected species. Using natural language processing models, we develop a machine-learning pipeline, similar to other approaches reported in the literature, to connect molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. These representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17/0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29/0.59, and coefficients of determination of 0.88/0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets. The latent vectors learned by the model are rich mathematical objects that capture the underlying chemical relations and also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory, we identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. By training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry, in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.
